chapter: Chapter V - Of Offences Against Women and Children
text: Section 63: Rape. Summary: Defines rape as sexual intercourse or sexual acts committed against a woman in specified circumstances, such as against her will, without her consent, through coercion, through fraudulent inducement, or when she is unable to understand the nature of consent. The definition is gender-specific to women, and the specified circumstances are set out in the statute.

chapter: Chapter V - Of Offences Against Women and Children
text: Section 64: Punishment for rape. Summary: Punishes rape with rigorous imprisonment of not less than ten years, which may extend to imprisonment for life, and also liable to fine. The court may impose a fine that is to be paid to the victim as compensation.

chapter: Chapter V - Of Offences Against Women and Children
text: Section 65: Punishment for rape of a woman under sixteen years of age. Summary: Provides a harsher punishment for rape of a woman under sixteen years of age, with rigorous imprisonment of not less than twenty years, which may extend to imprisonment for life, or death, and also liable to fine. Verify the exact sub-section structure against the official text before relying on it.

chapter: Chapter VI - Of Offences Affecting the Human Body
text: Section 103(1): Punishment for murder. Summary: Whoever commits murder is punishable with death or imprisonment for life, and is also liable to fine.

chapter: Chapter VI - Of Offences Affecting the Human Body
text: Section 103(2): Murder by group on specified grounds. Summary: When a group of five or more persons acting in concert commits murder on grounds such as race, caste, community, sex, place of birth, language, personal belief, or any similar ground, each member of the group is punishable with death or imprisonment for life, and is also liable to fine.

chapter: Chapter XVII - Of Offences Against Property
text: Section 316: Criminal breach of trust. Summary: A person entrusted with property, or with dominion over property, commits criminal breach of trust if they dishonestly misappropriate it, convert it to their own use, or dispose of it in violation of a legal direction governing how the trust must be discharged. Punishment is imprisonment of up to five years, or fine, or both.

chapter: Chapter XVII - Of Offences Against Property
text: Section 318: Cheating and dishonest inducement to deliver property. Summary: A person commits cheating by deceiving another and thereby dishonestly inducing that person to deliver property. Cheating that dishonestly induces delivery of property is punishable with imprisonment of up to seven years, and also liable to fine.

chapter: Chapter XIX - Of Criminal Intimidation, Insult and Annoyance
text: Section 351: Criminal intimidation. Summary: A person commits criminal intimidation by threatening another with injury to their person, reputation, or property, or to someone they are interested in, with intent to cause alarm. Punishment is imprisonment of up to two years, or fine, or both. Where the threat is to cause death or grievous hurt, the punishment is imprisonment of up to seven years.

chapter: Chapter VI - Of Offences Affecting the Human Body
text: Commentary on BNS Section 103: Section 103(1) corresponds to Section 302 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860. The group-based provision in Section 103(2) is widely referred to as the mob lynching provision. This is a cross-reference for lawyers and users reading older judgments, not operative text.

chapter: Chapter XVII - Of Offences Against Property
text: Commentary on BNS Sections 316 and 318: Criminal breach of trust (Section 316) corresponds to Sections 405 and 406 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860. Cheating (Section 318) corresponds to Sections 415 and 420 of the IPC. Judgments decided under the IPC on these offences remain persuasive but the BNS text governs offences committed on or after 1 July 2024.

chapter: Chapter XIX - Of Criminal Intimidation, Insult and Annoyance
text: Commentary on BNS Section 351: Criminal intimidation corresponds to Sections 503 and 506 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860. This is a cross-reference, not operative text.

chapter: Chapter XVII - Of Offences Against Property
text: Commentary on IPC Section 420: The Indian Penal Code, 1860 was replaced by the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 effective 1 July 2024. Cheating with dishonest inducement to deliver property, formerly Section 420, is now covered by Section 318(4) of the BNS. This record is background only and should not be cited as operative law for offences committed on or after 1 July 2024.
